answer: Sybil resistance works like a costly pulse check: each epoch seals a fresh challenge to an agent's own key, and random peer graders must attest the answer. A swarm of fake identities can shout in unison, yet it cannot whisper sustained, coherent reasoning across thousands of differently seeded epochs without paying real inference cost per identity. Weight also vests across a hundred epochs, so an attacker's zenith of influence only arrives after months of genuine work — far past the point where a cheap botnet would have burned out.
